# Optimize commit / publish / release / docs / CI

## Context

The commit→release→publish→docs toolchain has one glaring gap and several redundancies:

- **No PR CI.** The only `pull_request` workflow (`changeset-check.yml`) just checks that a
  changeset exists. Build / typecheck / test / lint / gates run **only** at release-tag time
  (`release.yml`) — so broken code can merge to `main` and first fail during a docs deploy or a
  release. This is the biggest risk.
- **commitlint is dead config.** `commitlint.config.ts` + two `@commitlint/*` devDeps exist, but the
  `commit-msg` git stage is a no-op (no `.vite-hooks/commit-msg` file) and nothing in CI checks
  messages. Conventional commits are unenforced.
- **`release.yml` double-works.** `cut-release.ts` already runs build/check/test + publint + attw
  **scoped to the release set** before tagging; the pushed tag then re-runs the **full-workspace**
  `ready` + `gate:publint` + `gate:attw`, sequentially, regardless of release size.
- **`docs.yml` over-builds and over-deploys.** It runs on every push to `main` with no path filter
  and rebuilds the whole workspace (`vp run -r build`), even for pushes that don't touch the site.
- **`ready` is a fully sequential 7-step `&&` chain**; independent lint/validate steps never overlap.
- **`gate:repository` only runs at release time.** It landed on `main` after npm OIDC/trusted-publishing
  provenance broke — publishable `package.json`s lacked `repository.url`, which provenance requires.
  `scripts/release/check-repository-metadata.ts` now asserts every publishable manifest has
  `repository.url === "git+https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken.git"`, wired into `release.yml`
  (`vp run ready && gate:repository && gate:publint && gate:attw`, sequential). But it's the *last*
  place to catch the exact failure that broke production, and it's a pure manifest read (no build) — so
  it belongs at PR time too.

Goal: add the missing PR gate, enforce conventional commits, catch the provenance regression earlier,
and cut the redundant/sequential work — without breaking the `vp`-only CI constraint (no pnpm on PATH)
or publish provenance.

### Verified mechanics (load-bearing)

- vp's task cache is `node_modules/.vite/task-cache/` and stores task **outputs** as `.tar.zst`
  tarballs — so a cache **hit re-materializes the gitignored generated files** (`platforms/**/generated/`,
  `formats/components/generated/`, web-components `src/generated/`, etc.). This is why downstream jobs
  can replay `vp run -r build` as a fast cache-extract instead of a full rebuild.
- `vp run -F "<pkg>..." <task>` selects the package **and its dependencies** (pnpm-style closure;
  confirmed in `vp run --help`: `<pattern>...` = deps, `...<pattern>` = dependents, `<pattern>^...` =
  deps only). So the docs build can be scoped to `@pantoken/docs`'s subgraph.
- Git hooks: `core.hooksPath=.vite-hooks/_` (vp-managed, gitignored dispatcher). Human hook bodies live
  at `.vite-hooks/<name>`. The `_/commit-msg` dispatcher already exists and forwards `$1`, and `_/h`
  prepends `node_modules/.bin` to PATH — so dropping in `.vite-hooks/commit-msg` is auto-wired, no
  installer step.

---

## 1. New PR CI gate — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

Trigger: `pull_request` + `push` to `main`. Concurrency cancels superseded PR runs:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
```

**Job graph** — one `build` job warms the cache, everything else fans out `needs: build` so no cold
stampede. The union of jobs equals `ready` + publint + attw, parallelized; `ready` itself is never
called in CI.

- `build` (no `needs`): checkout → setup-vp → **cache save** → `vp run -r build`.
- `typecheck` (`needs: build`): restore → `vp run -r build` (cache-extract) → `vp check`.
- `test` (`needs: build`): restore → `vp run -r build` → `vp run -r test`.
- `lint` (`needs: build`): restore → `vp run -r build` → `lint:css`, `lint:js`,
  `validate:generated:only`, `lint:markdown` (sequential within the job; all cheap).
- `publint` (`needs: build`): restore → `vp run -r build` → `vp run gate:publint`.
- `attw` (`needs: build`): restore → `vp run -r build` → `vp run gate:attw` (slowest; isolated so it
  doesn't gate the others).
- `repository` (independent, **no `needs: build`** — pure manifest read): setup-vp →
  `vp run gate:repository`. Cheap; catches the provenance-breaking missing `repository.url` on the PR
  instead of at release.
- `commitlint` (independent, PRs only): `fetch-depth: 0` → setup-vp →
  `vp exec commitlint --from ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} --to ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }} --verbose`.

Every job: `voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1` with `cache: true, run-install: true` (the only install step;
provides `vp`, no pnpm needed).

**vp task-cache persistence** — path is the single subtree, restored **after** setup-vp so install
can't clobber it. The cache is content-addressed internally, so a stale restore only yields misses,
never wrong output.

- `build` job: `actions/cache@v4`, path `node_modules/.vite/task-cache`,
  key `vp-taskcache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml','vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}`,
  restore-keys `vp-taskcache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml','vite.config.ts') }}-`
  then `vp-taskcache-${{ runner.os }}-`.
- downstream jobs: `actions/cache/restore@v4` (read-only) with the same key + restore-keys.

## 2. Enforce conventional commits

- **New `.vite-hooks/commit-msg`** (committed, executable, no shebang — runner invokes `/bin/sh -e`,
  mirroring `.vite-hooks/pre-commit`):
  ```sh
  vp exec commitlint --edit "$1"
  ```
  `vp exec` resolves `commitlint` from `node_modules/.bin`; config already wired
  (`commitlint.config.ts` → `@commitlint/config-conventional`). Local feedback on every commit.
- **CI backstop**: the `commitlint` job in `ci.yml` (above) validates the PR commit range.

## 3. Scope `release.yml` to the publish set

Replace the full `vp run ready && vp run gate:publint && vp run gate:attw` with verification scoped to
exactly the release set. Reorder so the release-plan step runs **first** (it already emits
`.release-packages.txt` and `.release-plan.json`), then drive scoped gates from it:

- `vp run -F <release-set> build && vp run -F <release-set> check && vp run -F <release-set> test`
- `vp run gate:repository` — kept **unscoped** (all publishable manifests; it's a millisecond read and
  the provenance check must not be narrowed).
- `vp exec -F <publishable-set> publint` and the existing scoped `attw` invocation.

Build the `-F` list from the release plan (the full release set for build/check/test so packs are
complete; the publishable subset for publint/attw). Add the task-cache **restore** so the scoped build
hits `main`'s warmed cache. **Leave every publish/provenance step unchanged**: `setup-node` registry,
corepack pnpm, `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE`, `id-token: write`, the publish loop, the GitHub release.

Safety tradeoff (accepted): release.yml stops re-verifying packages outside the release set — that

locally. What actually ships to npm is still gate-verified against the exact publish set immediately

## 4. Optimize `docs.yml`

- **Path filter** so a deploy only runs when the site can actually change. Add `on.push.paths`
  (broad-but-correct, since the site is themed by generated token output from many packages):
  `docs/**`, `packages/**`, `formats/**`, `platforms/**`, `renderers/web-components/**`, `plugins/**`,
  `design/**`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`; keep `workflow_dispatch`.

- **Add the task-cache restore** (same config as ci.yml) so unchanged deps are cache hits.
- Keep `concurrency: { group: pages, cancel-in-progress: false }` (don't cancel a live publish).

input.content:
name: CI

# The PR gate: build, typecheck, test, lint, and the publish/provenance checks — everything `ready`
# plus the gates covers, split into parallel jobs. Runs on every PR and on pushes to main so a
# regression is caught before merge, not at docs-deploy or release-tag time.

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

# Supersede in-flight PR runs; let main runs finish.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:
  # vp's task cache stores task OUTPUTS as .tar.zst tarballs, so a cache hit re-materializes the
  # gitignored generated dirs. The `build` job warms it; downstream jobs restore and replay
  # `vp run -r build` as a fast cache-extract instead of a cold rebuild.
  VP_TASK_CACHE: node_modules/.vite/task-cache
  VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX: vp-taskcache-

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore/save vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r build

  typecheck:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r build
      - name: Typecheck
        run: vp check

  test:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r build
      - name: Test all packages
        run: vp run -r test

  lint:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Lint CSS
        run: vp run lint:css
      - name: Lint JS
        run: vp run lint:js
      - name: Validate generated output
        run: vp run validate:generated:only
      - name: Lint Markdown
        run: vp run lint:markdown

  publint:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r build
      - name: publint
        run: vp run gate:publint

  attw:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r build
      - name: Are the types wrong?
        run: vp run gate:attw

  repository:
    # Pure manifest read — no build needed. Catches a missing repository.url (which breaks npm OIDC
    # provenance) on the PR instead of at release.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

name: CI

# The PR gate: build, typecheck, test, lint, and the publish/provenance checks — everything `ready`
# plus the gates covers, split into parallel jobs. Runs on every PR and on pushes to main so a
# regression is caught before merge, not at docs-deploy or release-tag time.

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

# Supersede in-flight PR runs; let main runs finish.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:
  # vp's task cache stores task OUTPUTS as .tar.zst tarballs, so a cache hit re-materializes the
  # gitignored generated dirs. The `build` job warms it; downstream jobs restore and replay
  # `vp run -r build` as a fast cache-extract instead of a cold rebuild.
  VP_TASK_CACHE: node_modules/.vite/task-cache
  VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX: vp-taskcache-

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore/save vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-

        with:

          NPM_CONFIG_FORCE: "true"
          NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS: "true"
          PNPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS: "true"
        run: |
          while IFS= read -r pkg; do
            [[ -z "${pkg}" ]] && continue
            echo "Publishing ${pkg}"
            pnpm -F "${pkg}" publish --tag "${{ steps.dist_tag.outputs.dist_tag }}" --access public --no-git-checks
          done < .release-packages.txt

      - name: Build package release notes
        run: |
          node scripts/release/build-release-notes.ts \
            --tag "${RELEASE_TAG}" \
            --plan .release-plan.json \
            --out release-notes.md

      - name: Create GitHub release
        if: github.event_name == 'push' && steps.plan.outputs.publish_count != '0'
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}
          body_path: release-notes.md
          prerelease: ${{ steps.dist_tag.outputs.prerelease }}

name: Deploy docs

# Build the VitePress + TypeDoc site and publish it to GitHub Pages.
# Enable Pages first: repo Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source = GitHub Actions.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Let a running deploy finish; don't cancel it mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      - name: Configure Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v6

      - name: Generate token output
        # Regenerates every package's generated/ dir — the token JSON TypeDoc reads and the
        # CSS the site is themed with. Uses `vp` (from setup-vp), so the job needs no pnpm on PATH.
        run: vp run -r build

      - name: Build docs
        run: vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build
        env:
          DOCS_BASE: /
          DOCS_HOSTNAME: https://pantoken.iywahl.com/

      - name: Write custom domain file
        run: echo "pantoken.iywahl.com" > docs/.vitepress/dist/CNAME

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: docs/.vitepress/dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5

## The gate

- `pnpm run ready` — the pass/fail gate. It's a `vp` task DAG (`ready:all`), not a serial chain:
  `build:all` runs once, then `check:all` (`vp check`), `test:all` (`vp run -r test`), `lint:css`,
  `lint:js`, `validate:generated:only`, and `lint:markdown` fan out concurrently. Everything that reads
  generated output depends on `build:all`, so generation happens exactly once (no concurrent codegen
  race). Must pass before you're done.
- `pnpm run check:publish` — the publish gate (`gate:publish`): `gate:repository` (asserts every
  publishable manifest has the `repository.url` npm OIDC provenance needs), `gate:publint`, and
  `gate:attw`. Publint/attw depend on `build:all`; the repository check is a pure manifest read.
- **CI runs the same checks on every PR** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): `build` → parallel
  `typecheck`/`test`/`lint`/`publint`/`attw`, plus a `repository` job and a `commitlint` job that lints
  the PR's commit range. Jobs share a persisted vp task cache (`node_modules/.vite/task-cache`), so the
  `build` job warms it and downstream jobs restore it and re-materialize generated dirs from cache.
- **Commit messages are conventional-commit-linted** locally by the `.vite-hooks/commit-msg` hook
  (`vp exec commitlint --edit`) and in CI by the `commitlint` job.
- Release automation uses Changesets and package-tag workflows in
  `.github/workflows/release.yml`. That workflow verifies a clean build/typecheck/test + `gate:repository`,
  then scopes the pack-heavy `publint`/`attw` gates to exactly the publish set (the full `ready` already
  ran on the merge-to-main the tag points at).
- Use `pnpm run release:version` to apply package changelog/version updates, then
  `vp run release:changelog:root` to rebuild the strict chronological root `CHANGELOG.md` before
  creating package tags.
- Generated artifacts are gitignored and reproduced on build: `platforms/tokens/src/generated/`,
  `platforms/css/style.css`, each preprocessor's static file, and web-components `src/generated/`.
  `build:all` produces them before any gate that reads them runs.

# Build, release, and the docs site

## Use the `vp` toolchain, never pnpm directly

- `vp` / `vpr` / `vpx` are **global** bins. Run tasks via `vp run <task>`, execute bins via `vp exec
[-F <glob>] <bin>`.
- **Package scripts must never shell out to `pnpm`.** CI (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) provides `vp`
  via `voidzero-dev/setup-vp` but **not** `pnpm` on PATH, so a `pnpm run …` inside any script breaks
  the docs deploy with `pnpm: command not found`. Local dev has pnpm, so a top-level `pnpm run X` is
  fine — but scripts it calls must stay pnpm-free internally.
- `.css` formatting: `vp fmt` (oxc) is JS/TS/JSON only and no-ops on `.css`. Stylelint owns `.css` —
  `lint:css` runs `stylelint --fix`, wired into `ready` and the `vite.config.ts` `staged` hook.

## The gate

- `pnpm run ready` — build `-r`, `vp check`, test `-r`, markdown lint. Must pass before you're done.
- `pnpm run check:publish` — `publint`.
- Release automation uses Changesets and package-tag workflows in
  `.github/workflows/release.yml`.
- Use `pnpm run release:version` to apply package changelog/version updates, then
  `vp run release:changelog:root` to rebuild the strict chronological root `CHANGELOG.md` before
  creating package tags.
- Generated artifacts are gitignored and reproduced on build: `platforms/tokens/src/generated/`,
  `platforms/css/style.css`, each preprocessor's static file, and web-components `src/generated/`.
  `ready` runs `vp run -r build` before `vp check`, so generated files exist in order.

See `docs/internal/release-strategy.md` for the runbook, dist-tag mapping, prerelease flow, and npm
organization governance model.

## Linting CSS

Root `stylelint.config.js` runs error-only core rules plus `@cssdoc/stylelint-plugin`'s
`cssdoc/valid-doc-comments`; anchor-positioning props are ignored and `@scope` is allowed. A parallel
`eslint.config.js` runs `@cssdoc/eslint-plugin` (via `@eslint/css`) over the same `.css` (`lint:js`).
`lint:css` targets the web-components `src/**/*.css` sources and the generated components CSS.

## The docs site

`docs/` is a VitePress site (`@pantoken/docs`) with two locales — `root` (English, `/…`) and `hu`
(Magyar, `/hu/…`) — a symmetric prefix swap that VitePress's default routing already handles (don't
set a custom `i18nRouting`).

- **Translation layer is `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`.** `LOCALES[locale]` holds every localizable UI
  string (nav/sidebar labels, `editText`, the theme selector, VitePress chrome labels, and local
  search). `config.ts` expands these into per-locale `themeConfig` (search is the exception — it lives
  in the global `themeConfig.search.options.locales`). Add new UI strings here, never inline.
- **Block-level API translation.** `build-api-locales.ts` doesn't translate whole `.md` files — it
  runs `segment-markdown.ts` to split each generated page into blocks: `prose` (descriptions,
  remarks, `@example` captions, cssdoc table Description cells), `glossary` (section headings,
  stability-badge pills, table column labels), and `preserve` (code fences, signatures, breadcrumbs,
  token tables). Only prose carries a content key, so a page's prose survives the scaffolding churn
  (badge flips, token-value changes, signature edits) that used to bust a whole-file key. `glossary`
  blocks always go through the deterministic `GlossaryTranslationAdapter` (keyless, never cached);
  `preserve` blocks are emitted verbatim.
- **The committed cache carries the prose; CI serves it.** The translation memory
  (`docs/i18n-cache/hu.api.json`) is content-addressed and adapter-agnostic, so a claude-authored
  prose entry is served to a `glossary` build as a plain cache hit. The workflow: run
  `pnpm run docs:api:locales:claude` **locally** to author prose (a cold run is bounded to ~30–40
  batched `claude -p` calls, resumable via the memory's autosave), then commit `hu.api.json`. CI's
  `docs:build` runs the `glossary` adapter, which serves that prose from cache and only ever fills
  structural headings/labels. Brand-new prose that isn't cached yet passes through as English — the
  glossary **never** caches its own prose passthrough (that would permanently mask the block from a
  later claude run), so it stays a miss until claude authors it. Never wire `:claude` into CI.
- **Running the cold pass.** Each `claude -p` call cold-starts a full agent, and the dominant cost is
  the per-call bootstrap — loading MCP servers, plugins, and project settings — not the translation
  itself (it dwarfs even a small model's inference). So the `:claude` tasks pass
  `--model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources user`: a fast model, **no
  MCP**, and user settings only (keeps auth, drops project/local hooks). That cuts each call from
  minutes to a few seconds. Override by editing the task or exporting your own
  `DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND_ARGS` before a direct `node scripts/…` run (`DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND`
  overrides the `claude` binary itself). Either task logs progress (`… N/M labels + prose blocks
translated`) and saves the memory after **each** chunk, so it's resumable — a kill or crash keeps
  completed chunks and a re-run serves them from cache.
- **The cold pass is generation-bound, so it runs chunks concurrently.** Once MCP is stripped, the
  wall-clock cost is the model streaming translations, not startup — so `ClaudeCodeTranslationAdapter`
  runs up to `DOCS_TRANSLATION_CONCURRENCY` (default 5) `claude -p` calls at once. Prose is batched at
  `DOCS_TRANSLATION_BATCH_BUDGET` chars/request (default 4k) — small enough that each JSON response
  stays reliable and progress is fine-grained, with the pool hiding the per-call startup. A chunk that
  errors is logged and skipped (its blocks stay uncached and retry next run), never sinking the whole
  run. Raise concurrency for more speed if you're not rate-limited; lower the budget if a run trips the
  per-item fallback (the model dropping a key from a large response).

## The cssdoc integration

pantoken consumes `@cssdoc/*` from **npm** (catalog entries; consumers use `catalog:`), not a local
workspace link. `docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts` is a thin wrapper: it builds pantoken's `resolveToken`
(syntax + value + local vars) and `resolveDemo` hooks, then calls `@cssdoc/typedoc`'s `emitCssApi`,
and keeps the `unknownReferences` drift guard. All page/index/sidebar rendering lives in
`@cssdoc/markdown`. The live `<div class="css-example">` preview is pantoken's own
`@pantoken/typedoc-plugin-live-example`, kept out of `@cssdoc/markdown` so the upstream stays generic.

**Catalog gotcha:** cssdoc packages reference `catalog:` deps; if cssdoc adds a new one, pantoken's
catalog must carry it too, or install fails with `ERR_PNPM_CATALOG_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND_FOR_SPEC`.

## The nested-`vp`-spawn limitation

Under `vpr docs:dev`, VitePress runs _under_ `vp`. Any `vp run …` / `vp pack` spawned from **inside**
that process dies with `Failed to spawn process: Invalid argument (os error 22)` on a cache miss. A
direct `node scripts/x.ts` is unaffected. So:

- The docs orchestrator's `upstream[].build` uses `["node","scripts/generate.ts"]` (cwd = the package
  dir), not a nested `vp run`.
- The CSS-API node runs `["node","scripts/build-css-api.ts"]` (cwd `docs`).
- `@pantoken/web-components`' `register()` bundle genuinely needs `vp pack` (which also can't nest), so
  it's not in the live orchestrator — rebuild it in a separate top-level shell
  (`vpr @pantoken/web-components#build`); `outputWatchPaths` on its `dist` bridges the change into HMR.

A `vp run X && vp run Y` chain _inside_ a package.json script is fine — that's a top-level
script-runner context, not a spawn from within the running VitePress process.

# Agents

Custom agent personas for the pantoken workspace. Start from `CLAUDE.md` for orientation and the
knowledge map. Each persona below pairs with deeper docs:

- Pipeline, IR, emitters → `docs/architecture/overview.md`
- Components → `docs/conventions/authoring.md`
- Web components → `docs/conventions/web-components.md`
- Build, release, docs site → `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md`
- Known gotchas → `docs/engineering-log.md`

## Core / pipeline

Owner of the transform and the emitter contract.

### Expertise

- `@pantoken/core` — resolves the Tokens Studio graph into the canonical `@property`-aligned `Token[]`
  IR (icons as `<image>` tokens); `toStyleDictionary()` for the native path.
- `@pantoken/model` — zero-dependency type contracts.
- `@pantoken/tokens` — vendors the IR + raw JSON as static files.
- `@pantoken/utils` — the shared `makeResolver`/`resolveTokens`, typed regexes, and the drift harness
  (`unknownReferences`, `danglingReferences`).
- `@pantoken/plugin-kit` — `definePlugin`, `extendPlugin`/`mergePlugin`, `checkPlugins`.

### Instructions

- Never make an emitter or web package depend on `core` — depend on `model` (types) + `tokens` (IR),
  or they'll transitively pull the GitHub-only upstream. See the upstream-decoupling section in the
  overview.
- Keep `utils` below `components` — `utils` must not import from `components`.
- Author plugins with `definePlugin` (dogfood); the factory infers capabilities from the hooks.

## Components

Owner of `@pantoken/components` (the semantic RSCSS CSS API) and its InstUI-parity work.

### Expertise

- Per-record source: `formats/components/src/{components,utilities,rules,declarations}/<name>.ts` +
  bucket `index.ts` registries; shared helpers in `src/lib/`.
- The modifier convention: key-value RSCSS compounds (`.instui-button.-color-secondary`,
  `-size-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}`), booleans as the prop name, default-on booleans inverted (`-without-*`).
- Auto-discovered deprecated aliases (authored in record metadata, cloned by `withAliases`); size
  twins via `withSizeAliases`.
- `@scope`/child-combinator scoping for nested element classes.
- Elevation and focus-outline are baked in (elevation into `components.css`, focus into `base.css`);
  fonts ship as opt-in `fonts.css`.

### Instructions

- Author records with `defineComponent`/`defineUtility`/`defineRule`/`defineDeclaration`. The doc
  comment is plain-string metadata; only the `css` body stays a template literal — tag it with
  `css` and add a `// prettier-ignore` line (oxfmt corrupts interpolated selectors otherwise).
- A deprecated modifier must be a **functional alias**, never a doc-only noop.
- Never name a modifier with a `-icon-` substring unless it's a real glyph — the generic
  `[class*="-icon-"]::before` painter will render a broken square on it.
- Per component, update the record, the drift-checked test, the guide, and a demo; then `vp check
--fix`, tests, `check:publish`, and `lint:markdown`. Browser-verify visual changes.
- Full authoring rules live in `docs/conventions/authoring.md`.

## Web components

Owner of `@pantoken/web-components` — the shadow-DOM custom elements.

### Expertise

- Co-located `src/**/*.css` shadow CSS is imported with `?inline`; `@tsdown/css` processes and
  minifies it into the JavaScript bundle, stripping `/** … */` doc comments before inlining.
- `register(target?, { prefix })` with a prefix-scoped registry adapter; `DEFAULT_PREFIX = "instui"`.
- The JS-behavior tier (tooltip, drilldown, pages, drawer-layout, interactive calendar, date/datetime
  pickers) built on the Invoker Commands API with a click-delegate fallback.
- `foundationCss()` injected once into `document.head` so elevation + focus tokens reach shadow roots.

### Instructions

- Keep the runtime graph Node-free (this bundles into the browser). Value imports of postcss-based
  `@cssdoc/*` are forbidden here; type-only is fine.
- To add an element: new `src/elements/<name>.ts` exporting an `ElementDefinition`, then add it to
  `DEFINITIONS` and `ELEMENTS` in the same (load-bearing) order — a test asserts the order.
- Behavioral shadow-DOM tests aren't possible without a DOM env; verify behavior in a real browser.
- Full rules live in `docs/conventions/web-components.md`.

## Docs and build

Owner of the VitePress docs site, i18n, the cssdoc integration, and the release gate.

### Expertise

- `docs/` VitePress site (`@pantoken/docs`), two locales (`root` English, `hu` Magyar) with a
  symmetric prefix swap; translation layer in `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`.
- The cssdoc integration: pantoken consumes `@cssdoc/*` from npm; `docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts`
  builds the `resolveToken`/`resolveDemo` hooks and calls `emitCssApi`.
- The `vp`-only pipeline and the nested-`vp`-spawn limitation (the docs orchestrator uses direct
  `node` builds).
- The gate: `pnpm run ready` + `pnpm run check:publish`.

### Instructions

- Package scripts invoke the toolchain via `vp` (`vp run`, `vp exec`), never `pnpm` — CI has no
  `pnpm` on PATH.
- Localizable UI strings go in `i18n.ts`, never inline. Use the `glossary` adapter for the generated
  API tree and the `claude-code` adapter only for hand-written guides.
- The docs orchestrator and CSS-API node spawn `node scripts/x.ts`, not a nested `vp run`.
- Full rules live in `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md`.

The `ready:all` command is running through its test phase with a cache miss since I modified package.json and vite.config.ts, so it's executing the full build and test cycle. While that's in progress, I'm confident the config loaded correctly since the earlier command succeeded, so there's no parsing conflict to worry about.

Now I'm thinking through a couple of correctness details in the CI workflow I set up. The commitlint job in ci.yml is guarded to only run on pull requests, so it won't try to access `github.event.pull_request.base.sha` on push events to main. And for the downstream jobs that run `vp run -r build` after restoring cache — if the cache is a full hit from the build job's sha-keyed entry, it'll extract outputs quickly. The key thing is that downstream jobs with `needs: build` will wait for the build job to fully complete, including its post-step cache save, so the cache will definitely be available when they run.

I'm also checking the release.yml filters syntax — the array gets expanded correctly as `-F a -F b` arguments to the attw task, which matches the gate:attw definition. And I removed the separate metadata step since the plan step now writes directly to GITHUB_OUTPUT, and I don't see target_private referenced anywhere else in the file anyway. For the docs.yml cache, it uses a docs-specific sha suffix but can fall back to the shared prefix, so it should be able to restore from the main build cache if needed. The lint job explicitly runs build before lint:css, but since lint:css depends on build:all, that explicit step becomes redundant — the dependency triggers the same build as a cache hit anyway. The test and typecheck jobs need explicit build steps since their tasks don't automatically depend on build — `vp run -r test` runs per-package tests that import generated code, and `vp check` needs the built output available. That's why I added the materialization step to those jobs, whereas lint already triggers build through its task dependencies.

For publint and attw, the explicit build is technically redundant since those gate tasks already depend on build:all, but I'm keeping them for clarity and safety. Több pantoken csomag generál fájlokat a build során — egy stíluslapot, egy `theme.json`-t, egy beágyazott token

## A `generated/` konvenció

Minden csomag, amely build műterméket állít elő, egy csomagonkénti `generated/` könyvtárba írja azt, és
semmi más nem él ott. Egyetlen szabály a `.gitignore` fájlban mindet lefedi:

```txt
**/generated/
```

Így nincs commitolt generált fájl — a build újra előállítja. Kétféle kimenet kerül oda:

- **Szállítható statikus fájlok** — olyan fájlok, amelyeket a felhasználó importál, például `@pantoken/css` `style.css` fájlja vagy
  `@pantoken/scss` `tokens.scss` fájlja. A csomag `exports` leképezése megtartja a nyilvános kulcsot
  (`"./style.css"`), de a `generated/` helyre mutat, így a fogyasztói API sosem változik.
- **Build köztes fájlok** — olyan fájlok, amelyeket a csomag saját forrása importál és bundlingol a `dist` mappába, például
  `@pantoken/tokens` beágyazott JSON-ja. Ezeket önmagukban nem publikálják; be vannak fordítva.

# Architecture overview

pantoken resolves Instructure UI's design tokens and icons once into a canonical model, then turns
that single model into many small, individually-publishable packages — plain CSS, SCSS/Less/Stylus,
React/Vue/Svelte/Angular, Tailwind/Panda/PostCSS, native Swift/Kotlin/Compose/Flutter, WordPress,
Drupal, Figma, and more. You install the smallest package that fits, or the unified `pantoken` meta
package that re-exports them all.

## The pipeline

`@pantoken/core` (the transformer) resolves the Tokens Studio graph into a canonical,
`@property`-aligned `Token[]` IR — icons rolled in as `<image>` tokens. `@pantoken/tokens` vendors
that IR plus the raw JSON as static files. Every emitter (`css`, `icons`, `astro`, `rehype`,
`swift`, and the rest) consumes the vendored IR. The native path runs `core.toStyleDictionary()`
→ `@pantoken/sd-config` (Style Dictionary v5) → `@pantoken/swift` / `@pantoken/cli`.

## The upstream-decoupling constraint (the load-bearing rule)

`@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` is GitHub-only — no npm publish, no types. `@pantoken/core`
depends on it. So a package that depended on `core` would transitively pull the GitHub-only upstream
into every consumer's install. To prevent that:

- Type contracts live in a zero-dependency **`@pantoken/model`**.
- Web and emitter packages depend on **`model` + `tokens`** (both upstream-free), **never on `core`**.
- `core` carries an ambient `declare module "@instructure/instructure-design-tokens"` shim, since the
  upstream ships no types.

When you add a package, keep it off `core` unless it genuinely runs the transform. Reach for `model`
(types) and `tokens` (the vendored IR) instead.

## Workspace layout — organized by how you consume each package

The axis is consumption, not language. The rule of thumb: **import the output → `formats/`;
generate it into another ecosystem → `platforms/`.**

| Bucket       | What lives here                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `packages/`  | Core machinery: `model` (types, zero-dep), `core` (transformer), `utils` (shared resolver + drift helpers), `plugin-kit` (the plugin factory), `cli`, and `pantoken` (the auto-generated meta package).                                                                  |
| `formats/`   | Importable npm serializations of the IR — `tokens`, `css`, `icons`, `dtcg`, `scss`, `less`, `stylus`, `icon-font`, and `components`. You `npm i` and import these.                                                                                                       |
| `platforms/` | Foreign-ecosystem source you _generate_ via the CLI and publish to that ecosystem's registry — `swift`, `android`, `compose`, `flutter`, `wordpress`, `vanilla`, `drupal`, `jekyll`, `hugo`, `email`.                                                                    |
| `renderers/` | Integrations that produce UI — `web-components`, `react`/`vue`/`svelte`/`angular` wrappers, `react-markdown`, `rehype`, `astro`, `pendo`, and CSS-var bridges (`shadcn`, `bootstrap`, `docusaurus`, `vitepress`).                                                        |
| `bundlers/`  | Build-pipeline integrations — `vite`, `tailwind`, `postcss`, `next`, `webpack`, `panda`.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `design/`    | Design-tool assets — `figma` (Variables payload) and `swatches` (ASE/GPL/sketchpalette).                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `plugins/`   | Split by kind: `plugins/pantoken/*` are `PantokenPlugin`s (colors, focus/simple-icons/stacking/transition/visual-debug/primitives/logos); `plugins/postcss/*` are PostCSS plugins (prune-custom-props); `plugins/typedoc/*` and `plugins/vite/*` are docs/build tooling. |
| `tools/`     | Internal build tooling — `sd-config` (Style Dictionary, powers the native targets), `aggregate` (builds the meta package).                                                                                                                                               |
| `ai/`        | Consumer-facing agent assets (`@pantoken/ai`, `pantoken-ai`) — NOT for developing pantoken itself. It drops AGENTS.md, llms.txt, and editor rules into a _consumer_ repo.                                                                                                |

## The meta package

`pantoken` is auto-generated by `tools/aggregate`, which scans each package's
`"pantoken": { key, kind }` field. `kind` decides how a package joins the meta:

- `namespace` — eager barrel + subpath.
- `sideEffect` — barrel + an `/inject` subpath.
- `subpath` — subpath only, kept **out** of the eager barrel. Used for heavy React integrations (e.g.
  `react-markdown`, tailwind, panda) so `import "pantoken"` never pulls React or a build config.

`aggregate` only _writes_ the meta. When you remove a package from the meta, delete its orphaned
`packages/pantoken/src/<name>.ts` by hand — aggregate won't.

## Shared helpers

`@pantoken/utils` (deps: `model` + `arkregex`) holds the formerly copy-pasted resolver:
`makeResolver(base, {mode?, overrides?})` (a `var()` + `light-dark()` resolver) and `resolveTokens`,
plus the typed `VAR_RE`/`LIGHT_DARK_RE` regexes, `camelCase`, and `parseHexColor`. It also holds the
drift/validation harness — `unknownReferences(text, ir)` (bridge targets must be real tokens) and
`danglingReferences(css)` (self-containment: every `var()` has a definition in the same output) — plus
the generic token→class engines `colorUtilitiesCss` and `tokenUtilitiesCss`. `utils` must never import
from `components` (it sits below it). `checkPlugins` (the capability guard) lives in `plugin-kit`, not
`utils`.

## The gate

`pnpm run ready` (build `-r` + `vp check` + test `-r` + markdown lint) must pass; `pnpm run
check:publish` runs publint. Generated artifacts (`platforms/tokens/src/generated/`,
`platforms/css/style.css`, each preprocessor's static file, web-components `src/generated/`) are
gitignored and reproduced on build.

## Deliberate boundaries

- **canvas-ios and canvas-android get no dedicated targets** — both already self-generate from InstUI
  through their own Style Dictionary pipelines. pantoken's generic swift/android/compose cover the
  general native case; duplicating their in-repo scripts would drift.
- **Storybook is a renderer, not a design tool** — pantoken themes the Storybook _app_; it doesn't
  author design variables (that's Figma). The test is "theming the app" vs "providing
  design-authoring assets."
- **Go was declined** — no real Go UI consumer worth a target.

## What I did

Everything's on branch `optimize-ci-release-hooks` (I branched off `main`, no commits yet).

**1. New PR CI gate — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`** (was missing entirely)
Parallel jobs — `build` → `typecheck`/`test`/`lint`/`publint`/`attw`, plus independent `repository` and `commitlint` jobs. The real issue is that `changeset status` needs to compare against `main`, but in the CI environment, `main` isn't available as a local branch since the checkout only fetches the PR head as a shallow single-branch clone. I need to look at how the `changeset-check.yml` workflow handles this checkout configuration. The simplest fix is to add a git fetch step that creates a local `main` branch tracking the remote, since `changesets` needs to resolve `main` locally when running `git merge-base` or similar commands to find diverged commits. Even with `fetch-depth: 0`, the base branch ref won't exist unless explicitly fetched. Let me look at the require-changeset job in changeset-check.yml to understand what needs fixing. The job checks out the code with full history, sets up the build environment, and runs the release verification command — but it's missing the git fetch for the main branch that changesets needs to compare against.

I need to add a step that fetches the base branch (main on pull requests) as a local branch so the changeset diff can work properly. Since this job only runs on pull_request events, github.base_ref will always be main, so I can fetch origin/main into a local main branch before the verification step runs. The `+` prefix forces the update, so it'll create or overwrite the local `main` branch from origin. Since the checkout action leaves us in detached HEAD state on the PR merge ref, there's no conflict with an existing `main` branch. Now I'm wondering whether I should actually be modifying changeset-check.yml or if this scope creep goes beyond what the user asked for.

Actually, this workflow is broken—it can't diff against main because the branch doesn't exist locally. That's a real defect blocking the PR, so fixing it is definitely in scope. Let me pull up the current changeset-check.yml file and add the fetch step.

name: Changeset check

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  detect-release-impact:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      release_impact: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.release_impact }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Detect release-impacting changes
        id: filter
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@v4
        with:
          filters: |
            release_impact:
              - 'packages/**'
              - 'formats/**'
              - 'platforms/**'
              - 'renderers/**'
              - 'bundlers/**'
              - 'design/**'
              - 'plugins/**'
              - 'ai/**'
              - 'tools/**'
              - 'package.json'
              - 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'
              - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'

  require-changeset:
    needs: detect-release-impact
    if: needs.detect-release-impact.outputs.release_impact == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      - name: Verify release metadata
        run: vp run release:status

  docs-and-internal-only:
    needs: detect-release-impact
    if: needs.detect-release-impact.outputs.release_impact != 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Skip changeset requirement
        run: |
          echo "No release-impacting files changed."
          echo "Changeset requirement is skipped for docs/internal-only PRs."

        with:

          # Full history so the changed-packages diff can reach the PR base / previous push.

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:

          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r build
      - name: Resolve changed packages
        id: changed
        env:
          CHANGED_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
        run: node scripts/release/changed-packages.ts
      - name: publint (scoped to changed packages)
        shell: bash
        env:
          SCOPE: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.scope }}
          PACKAGES: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.packages }}
        run: |
          if [[ "${SCOPE}" == "none" ]]; then
            echo "No publishable packages changed; skipping publint."
            exit 0
          fi
          if [[ "${SCOPE}" == "all" ]]; then
            vp run gate:publint
            exit $?
          fi
          filters=()
          IFS=',' read -ra pkgs <<< "${PACKAGES}"
          for p in "${pkgs[@]}"; do [[ -n "${p}" ]] && filters+=("-F" "${p}"); done
          echo "publint scoped to: ${pkgs[*]}"
          vp exec "${filters[@]}" publint

  contents: read

# Build, release, and the docs site

## Use the `vp` toolchain, never pnpm directly

- `vp` / `vpr` / `vpx` are **global** bins. Run tasks via `vp run <task>`, execute bins via `vp exec
[-F <glob>] <bin>`.
- **Package scripts must never shell out to `pnpm`.** CI (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) provides `vp`
  via `voidzero-dev/setup-vp` but **not** `pnpm` on PATH, so a `pnpm run …` inside any script breaks
  the docs deploy with `pnpm: command not found`. Local dev has pnpm, so a top-level `pnpm run X` is
  fine — but scripts it calls must stay pnpm-free internally.
- `.css` formatting: `vp fmt` (oxc) is JS/TS/JSON only and no-ops on `.css`. Stylelint owns `.css` —
  `lint:css` runs `stylelint --fix`, wired into `ready` and the `vite.config.ts` `staged` hook.

## The gate

- `pnpm run ready` — the pass/fail gate. It's a `vp` task DAG (`ready:all`), not a serial chain:
  `build:all` runs once, then `check:all` (`vp check`), `test:all` (`vp run -r test`), `lint:css`,
  `lint:js`, `validate:generated:only`, and `lint:markdown` fan out concurrently. Everything that reads
  generated output depends on `build:all`, so generation happens exactly once (no concurrent codegen
  race). Must pass before you're done.
- `pnpm run check:publish` — the publish gate (`gate:publish`): `gate:repository` (asserts every
  publishable manifest has the `repository.url` npm OIDC provenance needs), `gate:publint`, and
  `gate:attw`. Publint/attw depend on `build:all`; the repository check is a pure manifest read.
- **CI runs the same checks on every PR** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): `build` → parallel
  `typecheck`/`test`/`lint`/`publint`/`attw`, plus a `repository` job and a `commitlint` job that lints
  the PR's commit range. Jobs share a persisted vp task cache (`node_modules/.vite/task-cache`), so the
  `build` job warms it and downstream jobs restore it and re-materialize generated dirs from cache.
- **Commit messages are conventional-commit-linted** locally by the `.vite-hooks/commit-msg` hook
  (`vp exec commitlint --edit`) and in CI by the `commitlint` job.
- Release automation uses Changesets and package-tag workflows in
  `.github/workflows/release.yml`. That workflow verifies a clean build/typecheck/test + `gate:repository`,
  then scopes the pack-heavy `publint`/`attw` gates to exactly the publish set (the full `ready` already
  ran on the merge-to-main the tag points at).
- Use `pnpm run release:version` to apply package changelog/version updates, then
  `vp run release:changelog:root` to rebuild the strict chronological root `CHANGELOG.md` before
  creating package tags.
- Generated artifacts are gitignored and reproduced on build: `platforms/tokens/src/generated/`,
  `platforms/css/style.css`, each preprocessor's static file, and web-components `src/generated/`.
  `build:all` produces them before any gate that reads them runs.

See `docs/internal/release-strategy.md` for the runbook, dist-tag mapping, prerelease flow, and npm
organization governance model.

## Linting CSS

Root `stylelint.config.js` runs error-only core rules plus `@cssdoc/stylelint-plugin`'s
`cssdoc/valid-doc-comments`; anchor-positioning props are ignored and `@scope` is allowed. A parallel
`eslint.config.js` runs `@cssdoc/eslint-plugin` (via `@eslint/css`) over the same `.css` (`lint:js`).
`lint:css` targets the web-components `src/**/*.css` sources and the generated components CSS.

## The docs site

`docs/` is a VitePress site (`@pantoken/docs`) with two locales — `root` (English, `/…`) and `hu`
(Magyar, `/hu/…`) — a symmetric prefix swap that VitePress's default routing already handles (don't
set a custom `i18nRouting`).

- **Translation layer is `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`.** `LOCALES[locale]` holds every localizable UI
  string (nav/sidebar labels, `editText`, the theme selector, VitePress chrome labels, and local
  search). `config.ts` expands these into per-locale `themeConfig` (search is the exception — it lives
  in the global `themeConfig.search.options.locales`). Add new UI strings here, never inline.
- **Block-level API translation.** `build-api-locales.ts` doesn't translate whole `.md` files — it
  runs `segment-markdown.ts` to split each generated page into blocks: `prose` (descriptions,
  remarks, `@example` captions, cssdoc table Description cells), `glossary` (section headings,
  stability-badge pills, table column labels), and `preserve` (code fences, signatures, breadcrumbs,
  token tables). Only prose carries a content key, so a page's prose survives the scaffolding churn
  (badge flips, token-value changes, signature edits) that used to bust a whole-file key. `glossary`
  blocks always go through the deterministic `GlossaryTranslationAdapter` (keyless, never cached);
  `preserve` blocks are emitted verbatim.
- **The committed cache carries the prose; CI serves it.** The translation memory
  (`docs/i18n-cache/hu.api.json`) is content-addressed and adapter-agnostic, so a claude-authored
  prose entry is served to a `glossary` build as a plain cache hit. The workflow: run
  `pnpm run docs:api:locales:claude` **locally** to author prose (a cold run is bounded to ~30–40
  batched `claude -p` calls, resumable via the memory's autosave), then commit `hu.api.json`. CI's
  `docs:build` runs the `glossary` adapter, which serves that prose from cache and only ever fills
  structural headings/labels. Brand-new prose that isn't cached yet passes through as English — the
  glossary **never** caches its own prose passthrough (that would permanently mask the block from a
  later claude run), so it stays a miss until claude authors it. Never wire `:claude` into CI.
- **Running the cold pass.** Each `claude -p` call cold-starts a full agent, and the dominant cost is
  the per-call bootstrap — loading MCP servers, plugins, and project settings — not the translation
  itself (it dwarfs even a small model's inference). So the `:claude` tasks pass
  `--model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources user`: a fast model, **no
  MCP**, and user settings only (keeps auth, drops project/local hooks). That cuts each call from
  minutes to a few seconds. Override by editing the task or exporting your own
  `DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND_ARGS` before a direct `node scripts/…` run (`DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND`
  overrides the `claude` binary itself). Either task logs progress (`… N/M labels + prose blocks
translated`) and saves the memory after **each** chunk, so it's resumable — a kill or crash keeps
  completed chunks and a re-run serves them from cache.
- **The cold pass is generation-bound, so it runs chunks concurrently.** Once MCP is stripped, the
  wall-clock cost is the model streaming translations, not startup — so `ClaudeCodeTranslationAdapter`
  runs up to `DOCS_TRANSLATION_CONCURRENCY` (default 5) `claude -p` calls at once. Prose is batched at
  `DOCS_TRANSLATION_BATCH_BUDGET` chars/request (default 4k) — small enough that each JSON response
  stays reliable and progress is fine-grained, with the pool hiding the per-call startup. A chunk that
  errors is logged and skipped (its blocks stay uncached and retry next run), never sinking the whole
  run. Raise concurrency for more speed if you're not rate-limited; lower the budget if a run trips the
  per-item fallback (the model dropping a key from a large response).

## The cssdoc integration

pantoken consumes `@cssdoc/*` from **npm** (catalog entries; consumers use `catalog:`), not a local
workspace link. `docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts` is a thin wrapper: it builds pantoken's `resolveToken`
(syntax + value + local vars) and `resolveDemo` hooks, then calls `@cssdoc/typedoc`'s `emitCssApi`,
and keeps the `unknownReferences` drift guard. All page/index/sidebar rendering lives in
`@cssdoc/markdown`. The live `<div class="css-example">` preview is pantoken's own
`@pantoken/typedoc-plugin-live-example`, kept out of `@cssdoc/markdown` so the upstream stays generic.

**Catalog gotcha:** cssdoc packages reference `catalog:` deps; if cssdoc adds a new one, pantoken's
catalog must carry it too, or install fails with `ERR_PNPM_CATALOG_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND_FOR_SPEC`.

## The nested-`vp`-spawn limitation

Under `vpr docs:dev`, VitePress runs _under_ `vp`. Any `vp run …` / `vp pack` spawned from **inside**
that process dies with `Failed to spawn process: Invalid argument (os error 22)` on a cache miss. A
direct `node scripts/x.ts` is unaffected. So:

- The docs orchestrator's `upstream[].build` uses `["node","scripts/generate.ts"]` (cwd = the package
  dir), not a nested `vp run`.
- The CSS-API node runs `["node","scripts/build-css-api.ts"]` (cwd `docs`).
- `@pantoken/web-components`' `register()` bundle genuinely needs `vp pack` (which also can't nest), so
  it's not in the live orchestrator — rebuild it in a separate top-level shell
  (`vpr @pantoken/web-components#build`); `outputWatchPaths` on its `dist` bridges the change into HMR.

A `vp run X && vp run Y` chain _inside_ a package.json script is fine — that's a top-level
script-runner context, not a spawn from within the running VitePress process.

publint:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Full history so the changed-packages diff can reach the PR base / previous push.
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r build
      - name: Resolve changed packages
        id: changed
        env:
          CHANGED_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
        run: node scripts/release/changed-packages.ts
      - name: publint (scoped to changed packages)
        shell: bash
        env:
          SCOPE: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.scope }}
          PACKAGES: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.packages }}
        run: |
          if [[ "${SCOPE}" == "none" ]]; then
            echo "No publishable packages changed; skipping publint."
            exit 0
          fi
          if [[ "${SCOPE}" == "all" ]]; then
            vp run gate:publint
            exit $?
          fi
          filters=()
          IFS=',' read -ra pkgs <<< "${PACKAGES}"
          for p in "${pkgs[@]}"; do [[ -n "${p}" ]] && filters+=("-F" "${p}"); done
          echo "publint scoped to: ${pkgs[*]}"
          vp exec "${filters[@]}" publint

  attw:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Full history so the changed-packages diff can reach the PR base / previous push.
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r build
      - name: Resolve changed packages
        id: changed
        env:
          CHANGED_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
        run: node scripts/release/changed-packages.ts
      - name: Are the types wrong? (scoped to changed packages)
        shell: bash
        env:
          SCOPE: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.scope }}
          PACKAGES: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.packages }}
        run: |
          if [[ "${SCOPE}" == "none" ]]; then
            echo "No publishable packages changed; skipping attw."
            exit 0
          fi
          if [[ "${SCOPE}" == "all" ]]; then
            vp run gate:attw
            exit $?
          fi
          filters=()
          IFS=',' read -ra pkgs <<< "${PACKAGES}"
          for p in "${pkgs[@]}"; do [[ -n "${p}" ]] && filters+=("-F" "${p}"); done
          echo "attw scoped to: ${pkgs[*]}"
          vp exec "${filters[@]}" attw --pack --profile strict --no-emoji --ignore-rules no-resolution cjs-resolves-to-esm

  repository:
    # Pure manifest read — no build needed. Catches a missing repository.url (which breaks npm OIDC
    # provenance) on the PR instead of at release.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Check repository metadata

Let me answer the release-tag question first, since it affects your plan — then dig into the three docs changes.

## Will a tag cut on the PR branch trigger the release workflow?

**Yes, it triggers it — but the tag won't be "on main," and that's the problem.** Git tags are refs to a commit, independent of branches. `release.yml` fires on `push: tags: "@pantoken/*@v*"` regardless of which branch the commit lives on, and it checks out the tagged commit (not main). So:

- A tag pushed from `optimize-ci-release-hooks` **will** run `release.yml`, building/publishing from the **PR-branch commit**, not main.
- If the PR is later **squash-merged**, main gets a *different* SHA. The tag stays pointing at the orphaned PR-branch commit — so the published version's commit isn't in main's history, and the root `CHANGELOG.md`/tag chronology won't line up with main.

Two other things worth flagging before you cut:

- **`@pantoken/docs` is `private: true`** — not publishable. Cutting it produces an empty publish set, so `release.yml` would run the gates, then **skip publish and skip the GitHub release** (`publish_count == 0`). It wouldn't actually exercise the npm publish path. If you want to test publishing, pick a publishable package; if you want to test the docs *site*, that's `docs.yml` (push to main), not `release.yml`.
- **Cleanest test paths:** either merge this PR to main and cut from main, or cut a **prerelease** (`--beta`/`next` dist-tag) to exercise the pipeline without touching `latest` — accepting the tag won't be on main until merged.

My recommendation: merge to main first, then cut a real (or `beta`) release from main. Want me to hold the release until merge?

const translateSidebar = (item: SidebarItem, translate: (text: string) => string): SidebarItem => {

## Translation + parity tooling investigation

### 1. What `check-locale-parity.ts` verifies today — and its drift blind spot

It is a **pure file/structure parity check**. It reads only the filesystem, never the translation cache or any content hash. Concretely it checks four things:

- **Required files exist** (`docs/scripts/check-locale-parity.ts:19-24`, 53-56): `index.md`, `hu/index.md`, `api/typedoc-sidebar.json`, `hu/api/typedoc-sidebar.json`.
- **Guide page-set parity** by basename (`:58-70`): every `docs/guide/*.md` has a `docs/hu/guide/*.md` and vice-versa.
- **API tree parity** exact, page-for-page (`:73-90`): the `.md` tree under `docs/api` equals the tree under `docs/hu/api`.
- **Hero action count** matches between `index.md` and `hu/index.md` (`:47-49`, 93-101), by counting `- theme:` lines.

**It cannot detect drift.** As its own header says, it catches "English-only additions that never reached the translation layer" — i.e. a *missing file*. But the HU files are always written by the pipeline (`build-api-locales.ts` clones every EN page, and untranslated blocks fall through as English), so a page that exists but whose prose is stale English still passes. There is no comparison of English content hashes against cached translation keys anywhere in this script.

### 2. How the cache keys work (content-addressed)

The single key function is in `docs/scripts/translation-memory.ts:35-37`:

```ts
export function keyFor(kind: string, source: string): string {
  return createHash("sha256").update(`${kind} ${source}`).digest("hex");
}
```

Three `kind`s exist (`translation-memory.ts:24-29`): `"markdown"` (whole guide file), `"prose"` (an API prose block), `"text"` (a sidebar label). The cache file is `{ version: 1, entries: Record<hash, translation> }` (the JSON you saw in `hu.api.json` / `hu.guides.json`).

**Which keys *should* be present for the current English source:**
- **Guides** (`translate-guides.ts:41-49`): for each `docs/guide/<page>.md`, `keyFor("markdown", source)`.
- **API markdown** (`build-api-locales.ts:135-151`): `segmentMarkdown(file)` → `collectUnits(segments)` → keep `kind==="prose"` units → `keyFor("prose", block)`. (`glossary` units are **not** keyed — they run through the deterministic `GlossaryTranslationAdapter`, "keyless, never cached".)
- **API sidebars** (`build-api-locales.ts:167-179`): each label → `keyFor("text", label)`.

**A missing key means untranslated/drifted.** Two design points make absence a reliable drift signal:
- `TranslationMemory.save()` prunes the cache to exactly the keys *used* this run (`translation-memory.ts:84-94`), so a committed cache = exactly the keys of the English source at author time. Edit the English, its hash changes, the old entry no longer matches → effectively a miss.
- The **poison-cache guard** (`translation-memory.ts:157-166` and `204-209`) guarantees the glossary/passthrough of prose is *never* stored. So a prose key present in `hu.api.json` always means a real (claude) translation exists; absence = genuinely untranslated.

**Is there already an "expected vs cached keys" function? No.** The diff happens *inside* `translateUnits` at build time (`translation-memory.ts:120-132` — `memory.get` per unit), but it is not exposed as a standalone, adapter-free "what's expected vs what's cached" comparison. The building blocks exist and are all pure/importable: `segmentMarkdown` + `collectUnits` (`segment-markdown.ts:124-200`), `keyFor`, and `TranslationMemory.load(locale, namespace)` which exposes the entry map. There is no public getter for the raw key set, but `.get(kind, source)` returns `undefined` on a miss, which is enough for a checker.

### 3. What a "drift check" would concretely compare, and where it lives

For each namespace, compute the **expected key set from current English** and assert it's a subset of the **cached key set**:

- **Guides**: for every `docs/guide/*.md`, expected key = `keyFor("markdown", source)`; assert present in `hu.guides.json`. This needs no code generation — the English source is committed.
- **API**: requires the generated EN tree (`docs/api/**`, produced by `docs:api:en`/TypeDoc) to exist first. Then per generated `.md`: `collectUnits(segmentMarkdown(src))`, keep `prose`, expected key = `keyFor("prose", text)`; plus every sidebar label → `keyFor("text", label)`; assert each is in `hu.api.json`.

The logic should **reuse `segment-markdown.ts` (`segmentMarkdown` + `collectUnits`) and `translation-memory.ts` (`keyFor`, `TranslationMemory.load`)** so the checker keys content identically to the producer — any divergence would create false drift. Natural home: a new `docs/scripts/check-locale-drift.ts` (kept separate because API drift depends on generated output, whereas guide drift is pure), or a second pass inside `check-locale-parity.ts`. It must **not** import or instantiate any adapter.

### 4. How translations run locally, and what an "auto local" wrapper invokes

The two real-translation tasks set `DOCS_TRANSLATION_ADAPTER=claude-code`, which selects `ClaudeCodeTranslationAdapter` (`api-translation.ts:465-480`) — it shells out to the `claude` binary via `claude -p` (`api-translation.ts:431-462`). From `docs/package.json:13-15`:

```jsonc
"docs:api:locales:claude": "DOCS_TRANSLATION_ADAPTER=claude-code DOCS_TRANSLATION_CONCURRENCY=8 DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND_ARGS=\"--model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources user\" node scripts/build-api-locales.ts",
"docs:guides:locales:claude": "DOCS_TRANSLATION_ADAPTER=claude-code DOCS_TRANSLATION_COMMAND_ARGS=\"--model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources user\" node scripts/translate-guides.ts",
```

`build-api-locales.ts` regenerates the EN API itself (TypeDoc, badges, CSS API) before cloning + translating (`:107-122`), so it is self-contained. `translate-guides.ts` just reads `docs/guide/*.md`. Both write into the committed cache with autosave/resumability.

A **"run translations automatically locally" wrapper** would therefore just invoke both `:claude` tasks in sequence — something like `vp run docs:guides:locales:claude && vp run docs:api:locales:claude`. Confirmed, with the exact mechanism. The CI run is fully green now, and here's the `pack` diagnosis:

## Why `pack` misses in CI but not locally

Every miss says the same thing:

```
vp pack ○ cache miss: 'node_modules/.modules.yaml' modified, executing
```

- vp caches each package's `build` script (the repo uses `cache: true`, which enables script caching). The **compile** steps hit (`node scripts/generate.ts ◉ cache hit`), because they track *source* files.
- But `vp pack` auto-tracks the files it reads, which includes pnpm's **`node_modules/.modules.yaml`** (the installed-module manifest — pack resolves workspace deps through it).
- Every CI job runs `setup-vp` with `run-install: true`, and that reinstall **rewrites `.modules.yaml`**. So the pack fingerprint changes in every job → guaranteed miss. Locally there's no reinstall between runs, so pack replays from cache (we saw `vp pack ◉ cache hit` twice).

So: **build's compile is cached; `pack` is invalidated by the per-job reinstall, not by anything in your code.**

## What I found for fixing it — and my recommendation

I checked vp's config surface. There's **no global input-exclude knob** — `run.cache` only has `scripts`/`tasks` booleans. You *can* exclude `!node_modules/**` from a task's `input`, but only on `run.tasks` entries, and these are 70 per-package `build` *scripts*, not tasks. Converting all of them isn't worth it.

The two "real" fixes both lose:

- **Pass built `dist` as an artifact** instead of rebuilding downstream: eliminates the repack, but it's the brittle "enumerate every gitignored `generated/`/`dist` across 9 roots" approach the cache was chosen to avoid.

My recommendation: **accept it.** The repack is ~0.3–0.7s/package and the jobs run in parallel, so it's ~30–50s on the critical path of the full-build jobs. And the scoped-build change I just added means on a *typical* (non-global) PR, `attw`/`publint` only build the changed closure — so they barely repack at all. This PR looks expensive only because it changes root `package.json` (`scope: all`).

import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";

const docsRoot = join(import.meta.dirname, "..");
const apiIndexPath = join(docsRoot, "api/index.md");

const content = `# API reference

The pantoken API reference spans core libraries, format emitters, platform targets, renderers,
bundler plugins, and design tooling.

## Start here

| Area | Use this when you need... |
| --- | --- |
| [CSS API reference](/api/css/) | Component classes, utilities, rules, declarations, and token-backed CSS behavior. |
| [packages](/api/packages/) | Core contracts and pipeline helpers (model, core, utils, plugin-kit, CLI). |
| [renderers](/api/renderers/) | Framework-specific integrations (React, Vue, Svelte, Storybook, and more). |
| [platforms](/api/platforms/) | Generated platform outputs (Swift, Compose, Flutter, Android, WordPress, etc.). |

## Browse by group

| Group | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| [ai](/api/ai/) | Agent assets and AI tooling packages. |
| [bundlers](/api/bundlers/) | Bundler integrations for Next, Vite, Webpack, Tailwind, Panda, and PostCSS. |
| [design](/api/design/) | Design-surface outputs such as Figma and swatches. |
| [formats](/api/formats/) | Importable token/icon format outputs (CSS, SCSS, tokens, icons, and more). |
| [packages](/api/packages/) | Core package APIs that power the transform pipeline. |
| [platforms](/api/platforms/) | Generated target ecosystems and runtime-specific exports. |
| [plugins](/api/plugins/) | pantoken, Vite, PostCSS, and TypeDoc plugin APIs. |
| [renderers](/api/renderers/) | Framework and docs-site renderers and adapters. |
| [tools](/api/tools/) | Internal tooling APIs used by generation and docs pipelines. |
`;

writeFileSync(apiIndexPath, content);
console.log("✓ API overview: wrote docs/api/index.md");

name: Deploy docs

# Build the VitePress + TypeDoc site and publish it to GitHub Pages.
# Enable Pages first: repo Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source = GitHub Actions.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    # Only redeploy when the site can actually change. Broad on purpose: the site is themed by generated
    # token/CSS output from many packages, so a token or component change must trigger a rebuild.
    paths:
      - "docs/**"
      - "packages/**"
      - "formats/**"
      - "platforms/**"
      - "renderers/web-components/**"
      - "plugins/**"
      - "design/**"
      - "pnpm-lock.yaml"
      - "pnpm-workspace.yaml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Let a running deploy finish; don't cancel it mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      - name: Restore/save vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: node_modules/.vite/task-cache
          key: vp-taskcache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-docs-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            vp-taskcache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            vp-taskcache-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Configure Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v6

      - name: Generate token output
        # Builds only @pantoken/docs's dependency closure (the `...` suffix), not the whole workspace —
        # this regenerates the token JSON TypeDoc reads and the CSS the site is themed with. Uses `vp`
        # (from setup-vp), so the job needs no pnpm on PATH.
        run: vp run -F "@pantoken/docs..." build

      - name: Build docs
        run: vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build
        env:
          DOCS_BASE: /
          DOCS_HOSTNAME: https://pantoken.iywahl.com/

      - name: Write custom domain file
        run: echo "pantoken.iywahl.com" > docs/.vitepress/dist/CNAME

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: docs/.vitepress/dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5
