name: Deploy docs

# Build the VitePress + TypeDoc site and publish it to GitHub Pages.
# Enable Pages first: repo Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source = GitHub Actions.
#
# Gated behind CI: this runs after the CI workflow finishes on main and only deploys when CI passed,
# reusing the packages CI already built (downloaded as an artifact) instead of rebuilding the
# workspace. `workflow_dispatch` is the manual escape hatch — it builds the assets fresh (for a
# `[skip ci]` commit, or to re-run a failed deploy), since the CI artifact won't exist for it.

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["CI"]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read # download the build-output artifact from the triggering CI run
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Let a running deploy finish; don't cancel it mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Deploy only after a successful CI run (or a manual dispatch), and — for a CI-triggered run — only
  # when the pushed commit actually changed something the site renders.
  changes:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      should_deploy: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.should_deploy }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.ref }}
          fetch-depth: 2
      - name: Decide whether to deploy
        id: decide
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
            echo "should_deploy=true" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
            exit 0
          fi
          # The site is themed by generated token/CSS output from many packages, so treat those as
          # deploy-worthy too (broad but correct). Compare the pushed commit to its parent.
          if git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD | grep -qE '^(docs/|packages/|formats/|platforms/|renderers/web-components/|plugins/|design/|pnpm-lock\.yaml|pnpm-workspace\.yaml)'; then
            echo "should_deploy=true" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          else
            echo "should_deploy=false" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
            echo "No docs-relevant changes in this push; skipping deploy."
          fi

  build:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.should_deploy == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.ref }}

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      - name: Configure Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v6

      # Post-CI: reuse the workspace CI already built. Landing the artifact in place means the site
      # build below has the generated token/CSS output and the docs subgraph's dist without a rebuild.
      - name: Download build output from CI
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_run'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-output
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      # Manual escape hatch: the CI artifact doesn't exist, so build the docs dependency closure fresh.
      - name: Generate token output
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        run: vp run -F "@pantoken/docs..." build

      - name: Build docs
        run: vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build
        env:
          DOCS_BASE: /
          DOCS_HOSTNAME: https://pantoken.iywahl.com/

      - name: Write custom domain file
        run: echo "pantoken.iywahl.com" > docs/.vitepress/dist/CNAME

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: docs/.vitepress/dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5

name: Deploy docs

# Build the VitePress + TypeDoc site and publish it to GitHub Pages.
# Enable Pages first: repo Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source = GitHub Actions.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    # Only redeploy when the site can actually change. Broad on purpose: the site is themed by generated
    # token/CSS output from many packages, so a token or component change must trigger a rebuild.
    paths:
      - "docs/**"
      - "packages/**"
      - "formats/**"
      - "platforms/**"
      - "renderers/web-components/**"
      - "plugins/**"
      - "design/**"
      - "pnpm-lock.yaml"
      - "pnpm-workspace.yaml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Let a running deploy finish; don't cancel it mid-publish.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true

      - name: Restore/save vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: node_modules/.vite/task-cache
          key: vp-taskcache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-docs-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            vp-taskcache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            vp-taskcache-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Configure Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v6

      - name: Generate token output
        # Builds only @pantoken/docs's dependency closure (the `...` suffix), not the whole workspace —
        # this regenerates the token JSON TypeDoc reads and the CSS the site is themed with. Uses `vp`
        # (from setup-vp), so the job needs no pnpm on PATH.
        run: vp run -F "@pantoken/docs..." build

      - name: Build docs
        run: vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build
        env:
          DOCS_BASE: /
          DOCS_HOSTNAME: https://pantoken.iywahl.com/

      - name: Write custom domain file
        run: echo "pantoken.iywahl.com" > docs/.vitepress/dist/CNAME

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: docs/.vitepress/dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5

The docs build regenerates the API docs fresh via typedoc rather than relying on the artifact, which only contains the package build outputs, so there's no conflict between what's in the artifact and what docs:build produces.

The artifact's generated/ directory covers package-level outputs, not docs-specific generated content like docs/api (which typedoc creates) or the vitepress build output. The changes job's shallow fetch depth of 2 should work fine on main after a squash merge since HEAD~1 will exist. PR [#6](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/6) is **green** — 10 checks pass, 1 correctly skipped (`require-changeset`, since it's workflows-only). And it doubled as live proof the earlier scoping works: `attw`/`publint` finished in **27s** because this PR touches no publishable packages (`scope: none`).

## Summary

**PR #6 — gate docs behind CI + reuse its build:**
- `docs.yml` now triggers on `workflow_run` (after CI completes on main) and deploys only when CI **succeeded** — no more racing CI in parallel.
- CI's `build` job uploads its output (`generated/` + `dist/`) as an artifact (main only); the deploy **downloads it and skips the rebuild**, going straight to the VitePress/TypeDoc site build.
- `workflow_dispatch` stays as the escape hatch — no artifact, so it builds the docs subgraph fresh (for `[skip ci]` or a failed deploy).
- A `changes` gate keeps the path filter so non-docs pushes don't redeploy.

**One caveat worth calling out:** the `workflow_run` path can only be exercised once `docs.yml` is on `main` (GitHub evaluates `workflow_run` from the default branch). So after you merge #6, watch the *first* main push — that's the real end-to-end test of the artifact hand-off. The manual `workflow_dispatch` path is also worth a one-time run to confirm the fresh-build escape hatch. If the artifact turns out to miss anything the site build needs, the fix is a one-line glob tweak in CI's upload step.
